title.narrative: Humanitarian Assistance to Rat Flood Affected People in Rangamati district of Bangladesh

description.narrative: Every 48 years, the gregarious flowering of the Mitinga bamboo provides a sudden and massive food source for rats living in bamboo forests. As a result, these forests see an explosion in the rat population which, once the bamboo flowering ends, moves out of the forest into nearby fields and human settlements in search of food. This is known as a "rat flood". A rat flood started in September 2025 in Sajek Union (Rangamati District). It has caused severe damage to the annual "Jum" crop on which the target population, remote hill farmers from the Tripura and Chakma ethnic groups are totally reliant for their food security and livelihoods. As there is only one cropping cycle in this area, the loss of the crop leaves the communities extremely vulnerable both in terms of access to food, and the ability to plant during the next cycle. Caritas Bangladesh will provide 500 vulnerable households with 2 months of food, and cash to allow the purchase of agricultural inputs. To combat the spread of rat borne disease Caritas will also provide basic sanitary and hygiene awareness to 2700 people.
